text.p: Troy O'Leary homered twice and rookie Nomar Garciaparra had four hits and three RBI as the Boston Red Sox pounded the Texas Rangers 17-1 Tuesday.

O'Leary opened the scoring for the Red Sox in the second when he reached Jose Alberro (0-3) for the first of his two upper-deck shots to right field. His leadoff blast in the fourth gave him the second two-homer game of his career.
O'Leary became just the second player in history to homer twice in one game into the upper deck at Arlington Stadium. Former Ranger Mickey Tettleton did it last year.
"I just got lucky tonight," O'Leary said. "Our hitting had an outstanding night."

Garciaparra led off the third with a double and later drove in two runs with a single as the Red Sox sent 14 batters to the plate in the eight-run inning. He added an RBI double in Boston's four-run fourth before leading off the sixth with his 20th homer.
Wil Cordero had a three-run homer in the third.
Tom Gordon (6-9) allowed a run and three hits over six innings to snap a three-game losing streak. Kerry Lacy, John Wasdin and Jim Corsi added three innings of scoreless relief.
"I tried not to think about it (the lead)," said Gordon. "I didn't want to leave my game. I was just trying to stay focused and think about what I was doing out there."
Boston's 24 hits were an American League season high.
Fernando Tatis homered for the lone Texas run as the Rangers lost for the seventh time in their last eight games.
In Anaheim, Dave Hollins drove in three runs and Jason Dickson survived 5 1/3 rocky innings as the Angels edged the Milwaukee Brewers 6-5 for their eighth win in 10 games.
Dickson (11-4) allowed four runs and seven hits -- including three home runs -- for his third straight win. Troy Percival, Anaheim's fifth pitcher, threw 1 1/3 perfect innings for his 17th save.
Tony Phillips and Darin Erstad each had two hits and two runs for the Angels, who have won 22 of their last 29 games to remain tied with Seattle for the lead in the A.L. West.
For Milwaukee, Bryce Florie (2-3) allowed six runs and eight hits in five-plus innings. Dave Nilsson hit two home runs and Jeromy Burnitz homered for a club-record fifth straight game.
In Seattle, Russ Davis hit Terry Mathews' first pitch of the bottom of the ninth inning over the centre-field wall to give the Mariners a 4-3 victory over the Baltimore Orioles.
Davis, who came in 3 for his last 28, went hitless in his first three at-bats before blasting his 16th homer of the season.

Norm Charlton (3-7) pitched a perfect ninth, capping a strong effort by the much-maligned Seattle bullpen. Paul Spoljaric did not allow a hit and struck out two over 2 2/3 scoreless innings in relief of starter Omar Olivares.
The Mariners won their third straight following a four-game losing streak.
Baltimore, which suffered just its third loss in 14 games, had its lead in the A.L. East cut to 4 1/2 games over the Yankees.
In Kansas City, Kenny Rogers scattered six hits over five innings in his first start in more than seven weeks and the New York Yankees captured their seventh win in eight games, 4-1 over the Royals.

Rogers (5-4), who was traded to San Diego before Greg Vaughn failed a physical to nullify the deal, started for the first time since getting tagged for four runs and four hits in three innings against Florida on June 15. He gave up one run, walked two and struck out two.
Kevin Appier (6-10) took the loss.

In Detroit, Deivi Cruz had two hits, two RBI and scored the go-ahead run and Justin Thompson (10-8) won his second straight start as the Tigers held on for a rare win against the Cleveland Indians 6-4.
Batting ninth with a .223 average, Cruz figured in the first four runs for the Tigers, who gained a split of the two-game series with just their ninth win in 42 games against the Indians since 1994.
At Minnesota, Ed Sprague drove in three runs to lead the Toronto Blue Jays to an 8-3 victory over the Twins and a split of the two-game series.
Robert Person (5-7) allowed two runs and and five hits in seven innings for the win.
In Oakland, Doug Drabek allowed four hits over seven innings and Robin Ventura had a homer and scored twice as the Chicago White Sox defeated the Athletics for the eighth straight time, 3-0.
Drabek (8-7) walked one and struck out three as he won his second straight start. Nelson Cruz, Tony Castillo and Matt Karchner finished up Chicago's sixth shutout.
